sections.h2: Where to pay and ask questions
sections.html:
Levy County owners pay at the Tax Collector's main office in Bronson, 310 School Street, Suite 102 (352-486-5172), or at one of two branches. Valuation is handled by the Property Appraiser, whose office is also in Bronson, at (352) 486-5222.

  • Bronson main office: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson, FL 32621, open Monday to Friday from 8:30 to 4:30.
  • Williston branch: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, FL 32696, (352) 528-6091.
  • Chiefland branch: 226 North Main Street, Chiefland, FL 32626, (352) 493-4646.

No address change can be made at the collector's counter, whether the account is real property or tangible. Those go through the appraiser. A seller should update the mailing address there so a stray bill reaches the right person after closing.

sections.h2: Property tax dates in Levy County
sections.html:
Bills are due November 1, and a balance still open after March 31 becomes delinquent on April 1. The state discount starts at 4 percent in November and shrinks one point a month to 1 percent in February.

Reminder letters on unpaid accounts are sent by April 30. The delinquent list is prepared in May for the newspaper and the web, and the certificate auction usually runs by May 31. Chapter 197 requires it to start no later than June 1.

The earlier part of the year follows a fixed state calendar too: value is set as of January 1, exemption filings are due by March 1, a proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and a petition on value must be filed within 25 days of that notice.

sections.h2: Paying online or at the counter
sections.html:
Card payments online carry a fee and e-checks do not. The collector's site shows 2.3 percent on credit cards, a flat $1.75 for charges under $76, and nothing for an online e-check (ACH). The processor keeps those fees, not the county.

At the counter, each payment draws 2.3 percent and e-checks are unavailable. A payment processed after 11:59 p.m. counts as the next calendar day, which can trap someone near a deadline. A seller who wants a clean payoff can use an online e-check before midnight and avoid both the fee and the next-day rule.

Accepted cards are Visa, Master Card, American Express and Discover. If the system gives trouble, call 352-486-5172 on a weekday.

sections.h2: What happens when Levy County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent tax is sold as a certificate, which is a lien on the property rather than a transfer of the house. Its face amount adds up the unpaid tax, 1.5 percent a month for April and May, a 5 percent collector commission, the advertising charge and the cost of the sale.

Levy County tax certificate terms
Certificate termRule
Sale methodOnline auction through West Florida Business Systems, on or before May 31
Bid range0 to 18 percent in 0.25 percent steps, lowest rate wins
Minimum interest if redeemed on or after June 15 percent (not for zero bids)
Unbid certificatesIssued to the county at 18 percent
Certificate life7 years
Holder may seek a tax deedAfter two years from April 1 of the issuance year

The delinquent list runs weekly for three weeks before the auction. A certificate buyer must wait two years, counted from April 1 of the issuance year, before reaching out to the owner.

Someone applying for a tax deed has to complete these steps, and the fee amounts can change without notice:

  • File a signed tax deed application.
  • Redeem any other outstanding certificates and pay current tax if owed.
  • Pay a $150 title search fee and a $75 application fee.

The county clerk then schedules the sale and charges for advertising, mailing and sheriff costs.

When homestead is on the current roll, the opening bid adds half the assessed value to the taxes and costs. A parcel that draws no bids can join the list of lands available for taxes, and land left unsold there for 3 years reverts to Levy County. Unpaid government liens survive a tax deed under s. 197.552.

For an owner planning to sell, timing is what counts. Ask the collector for a payoff on any certificate before you list, because a title company will want every lien cleared at closing.

Farm classification belongs to the owner, not the land. The appraiser calls it non-transferable, so a buyer files a new application after any sale or transfer.

Filing runs January 1 through March 1. Under the statute the office cites, only land used mainly for bona fide agriculture, meaning good-faith commercial use, qualifies. Zoning alone earns nothing, and the use should be in place on the January 1 assessment date, or a reasonable effort to start it must have been made.

If you are selling acreage, tell the buyer which parcels carry the classification today. A buyer who fails to qualify can face a higher assessment. Denials are mailed to the applicant, who can ask the appraiser to talk it through.

sections.h2: How the certificate auction works for bidders
sections.html:
The sale is online through West Florida Business Systems, and the Tax Collector says no deposit is needed under the current format. Each bidder submits a Participating Bidder Agreement after registering or logging in, plus an electronic W-9 every year.

A practice system lets new bidders try things out, and bids made there do not carry to the live sale. A certificate can be resold to another buyer once the endorsement form and a $2.25 transfer fee per certificate reach the Tax Collector. The office cautions that a certificate is not a guaranteed investment, and one left without action through its seven-year life while the tax stays unpaid is cancelled. For you as the owner, the point is that a private investor holds the lien, cannot contact you for the first two years, and may then apply for a deed.

Levy County is rural, with about 48,520 residents across 1,118 square miles, up 13.1 percent since the 2020 count. Of 22,192 housing units, 81.4 percent are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied value is $190,600. Long tenure is common, which usually means a Save Our Homes assessment below market value that resets after a sale.

A Levy County deed carries Florida's 70 cents per $100 stamp tax. The clerk collects it at recording from whichever party the contract assigns, and every party stays liable.

sections.h2: Steps before selling with taxes owed
sections.html:
1. Call the collector for a current account balance and any certificate payoff.
  2. Confirm the mailing address with the appraiser.
  3. If the land is farmed, list which parcels carry agricultural classification.
  4. Give the closing agent the payoff letters so liens are cleared from your proceeds.

A cash buyer can close faster, but title work still turns up unpaid tax, so the payoff comes first either way.

faqs.q: Where is the Levy County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: The main office is at 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson. Branches are at 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, and 226 North Main Street, Chiefland. All keep weekday hours.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay Levy County property tax online?
faqs.a: Cards add 2.3 percent, or a flat $1.75 under $76, paid to the processor. Online e-checks are free, while payments at the office add 2.3 percent.

faqs.q: When does Levy County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1 after the bill year. Reminders go out by April 30, and the certificate auction normally wraps up by May 31.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my Levy County agricultural classification?
faqs.a: No. It is non-transferable, so the buyer files a new application by March 1 and must meet the bona fide agriculture test.

faqs.q: How soon can a tax deed be sought on unpaid Levy County tax?
faqs.a: A certificate holder may apply two years after April 1 of the issuance year. If your parcel has a certificate, ask the collector for a payoff figure.
